summary: The old harness has a preexisting XPath variable coverage gap: it always constructs queries without a variable set. The new depth limit does not remove that constraint. Full coverage of the selected changes remains unverified because decisive constructor and parser call paths were not supplied.

coverage_evidence.dependency_reason: The complete entry shows its sole query construction and cleanup.

claims.necessity_reason: Variable-backed query compilation is within the constructor's supported argument surface. A finite query such as $x can use a populated variable set, but the complete old entry always omits that argument. Its default is null, and the parser rejects variable references without a set. No other call in the entry supplies one.

before.requirement: When compiling an XPath expression that references a defined variable, pass a populated xpath_variable_set to the query constructor so the reference can compile.
before.reason: The constructor accepts a variable set, while the parser rejects a variable reference if no set is provided. The old harness calls the constructor with only the query text.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The variable-reference parser requires a supplied set and resolves the named variable from it.

after.requirement: When compiling an XPath expression that references a defined variable, pass a populated xpath_variable_set to the query constructor so the reference can compile.
after.reason: The constructor argument and variable-reference requirement remain present. The depth check does not supply the variable set omitted by the old harness.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The variable-reference parser still requires a supplied set and a matching variable.
Change g0012 adds expression-depth handling; it does not provide variables for expressions being parsed.

claims.comparison_reason: On both sides, the same one-argument constructor call uses the null default for the variable-set argument. The complete harness has no equivalent setup or call sequence.
